discovery: Evidence for the nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

motivation: In 2023, pulsar timing arrays reported the first evidence of the Hellings-Downs angular correlation in the arrival times of millisecond pulsars. This is the signature of a gravitational-wave background at nanohertz frequencies. It turned the Galaxy into a detector for gravitational waves about ten orders of magnitude lower in frequency than LIGO can reach. The result opened a new window on supermassive black-hole binaries across cosmic time and possibly on new physics in the early universe. It rests on decades of work to find millisecond pulsars, to build ultra-stable timing systems, and to develop rigorous noise-modelling and Bayesian methods. Maura McLaughlin co-founded NANOGrav and led its observations. Xavier Siemens led NANOGrav's analysis and detection strategy. Michael Kramer led the European effort and pioneered precision pulsar timing and relativistic tests. Together they made pulsar timing a working gravitational-wave observatory.
